oil.summary: Crude markets extended their blistering monthly rally—WTI +17.9% and Brent +16.4% over 30 days—with Brent pressing toward the $100 threshold at $97.23 as of settlement. The dominant driver remains Middle East risk: Iran has threatened fresh economic warfare and missile strikes, Houthis attacked Saudi energy sites forcing temporary operational halts in the southern border region, and Hormuz tensions persist even as Kuwait partially rerouted exports back to roughly 1 million bpd. China's crude buying rebounded for a second consecutive month in August, with fuel exports jumping 29%, removing a key demand cushion that had previously capped prices. The US temporarily eased Russia sanctions in a bid to cool prices, though the measure has riled European allies. RBOB gasoline cratered 4.96% on the day—a notable divergence—while heating oil held firm (+0.55%) as a diesel supply crunch is forecast to last through winter on refinery capacity shortfalls.
drivers: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities and persistent Hormuz tensions pushing Brent toward $100
China crude import rebound for second consecutive month adding renewed demand pressure
Global diesel/heating oil supply crunch expected to persist through winter due to refinery capacity gaps

gas.summary: European gas markets were the standout mover today, with TTF surging 6.60% on the day to €76.7/MWh—up nearly 10% on the week and an extraordinary 38% over the past month. The Middle East supply shock is spilling directly into European gas pricing, compounding an already fraught winter storage race. Germany's gas storage association has warned of shortage risk this winter if temperatures fall below recent norms, adding urgency to the buying. Henry Hub, by contrast, fell 3.26% to $2.878/MMBtu, reflecting a continued US-Europe pricing divergence driven by differing supply-demand dynamics. The headline data for LNG-specific flows or storage fill rates is limited in today's feed, but the direction of travel on the continent is unambiguously tighter.
drivers: Middle East supply shock driving TTF to multi-month highs, up 38% in one month
Germany's storage association warning of winter shortage risk if temperatures undershoot expectations
Sharp US-Europe gas price divergence: Henry Hub -3.26% on the day vs TTF +6.60%

power.summary: EU carbon allowances (EUA) added 1.67% to $81.165/EUA, extending a steady month of gains (+4.55%), as the broader energy tightness narrative—amplified by the TTF spike—raises the cost of gas-fired generation and supports carbon pricing. Vitol's CEO characterized global fuel markets as "tight and inflexible" despite higher Persian Gulf flows, a characterization that maps directly onto European power cost pressures. A headline noting Germany's power grid as a potential NATO vulnerability underscores longer-term structural concerns for grid resilience and investment. A US-Saudi nuclear cooperation deal cleared a Vienna procedural hurdle, though it remains under Congressional review and offers no near-term supply relief. The power-sector specific data flow today is relatively thin; the primary pricing signals are being transmitted through the TTF channel and the broader geopolitical risk premium.
drivers: TTF surge (+6.60% on the day, +38% monthly) lifting gas-fired generation costs and supporting EUA prices
Vitol CEO flagging global fuel markets as 'tight and inflexible,' reinforcing the risk-premium backdrop
Germany grid resilience concerns and US-Saudi nuclear deal in Congress review as longer-term structural factors
